$comment: The reviewed identity of the Windows build-input bundle (#236, W1-R). The publisher is TOLD what it may push; it does not publish whatever it happens to have built. W1-R-B compares the digest a trusted master build produces against this value and refuses on any difference, then verifies that the registry stored these exact manifest bytes. Regenerating the lock necessarily changes these digests — that is the point: a new toolchain is a new bundle and a new identity, never a mutation of this one.
$supersedes: sha256:7a29e83cbffd3b5829b429855eaa1c93d688d5b2cc2d17b2169ba9b83a4dff9a was the W1-R-A candidate. It is NOT preserved. W1-R-B added the signing trust root to the layer, regenerated the lock against databases that had moved, and picked up five upstream package revisions; each of those changes the bytes, so the identity changed with them. The old digest was never published and names nothing.
$pathsComment: 501 files are delivered in the layer; manifest.sha256 lists the other 500 because it cannot list itself. The two-build comparison diffs manifest.sha256, so it reports 500.
publishedNote: NOT PUBLISHED until W1-R-B dispatches the publisher from trusted master, the human reviewer approves the windows-build-input-publication deployment, and the stored manifest is read back and compared byte for byte.
